title: Product monograph headings, in order
text: The product monograph uses the numbered headings of the master template in order: 1 Indications to 12 Special Handling Instructions in Part I, 13 Pharmaceutical Information to 17 Supporting Product Monographs in Part II. The Patient Medication Information uses the plain-language headings of the template.
simplified: Subsections 7.1.1 to 7.1.4 sit directly under section 7 in the editor; the unnumbered body-system subheadings of section 7 are written in the text.

title: Required content is filled
text: Each required heading of the product monograph and the Patient Medication Information, and each mandatory item of the label, has content.
at: Master template; Food and Drug Regulations C.01.004

title: Title page
text: The title page gives "Product Monograph Including Patient Medication Information", the scheduling symbol before the brand name (Pr for a prescription drug), and the date of authorization in YYYY-MM-DD form.
simplified: The app checks the title, the symbol and the dates; the full title page also carries the sponsor, the control number and any trademark declaration.

title: Serious Warnings and Precautions box
text: When serious warnings were identified, section 3 holds them in a box of bulleted text, generally no more than 20 lines, with cross-references to the relevant sections, and the Patient Medication Information repeats them in plain language in its own serious warnings box.

title: Recent Major Label Changes
text: Each entry names the section and gives the month of approval in YYYY-MM form; entries are kept for 24 months.
at: Master template, Recent Major Label Changes

title: Standard Patient Medication Information statements
text: The Patient Medication Information opens with "READ THIS FOR SAFE AND EFFECTIVE USE OF YOUR MEDICINE", its Overdose box gives the poison control text with Health Canada's toll-free number 1-844 POISON-X (1-844-764-7669), and Reporting side effects gives the Canada Vigilance toll-free number 1-866-234-2345 and says the program does not provide medical advice.
simplified: The app checks the opening line, the telephone numbers and the medical-advice sentence rather than every word.

title: Pr symbol
text: A prescription drug shows the symbol "Pr" in the upper left quarter of the principal display panel; no other drug may show it.

title: Drug identification number
text: The principal display panel shows the eight-digit DIN with "DIN" (or "Drug Identification Number" / "Drogue : identification numérique").

title: Proper name at least half the size of the brand name
text: Where there is a brand name, the proper name is shown on the principal display panel in letters at least one half the size of the brand name.

title: Lot and expiry
text: The label shows the lot number (with "Lot") and the expiration date (with "EXP"), giving at least the month and year.
simplified: The app checks the prefixes and a month and year; the regulations do not fix a date format.

title: English and French
text: Information required on the label is shown in both English and French.
simplified: The app looks for French wording in the dosage form, net amount, directions, storage and reporting panels.

title: Contact for reporting side effects
text: Labels of drugs in dosage form give a way to contact a person in Canada (telephone, email, website or postal address) and state that suspected injuries can be reported to that person.
